about.title: Biggs Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Biggs is a small Butte County town, but the stores, gas stations, and public spaces along 5th Street, SR-99, and E Street still see plenty of foot traffic — and with that comes the occasional wet floor, cracked walkway, or poorly lit stairwell that a property owner failed to address. California law doesn't hand injured people an automatic win in these cases; you generally have to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why what happens right after a fall matters so much. Photos of the spot, names of witnesses, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage can make a real difference later. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result — we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who takes premises liability cases seriously and works on contingency, so there's nothing owed unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before you were hurt. An attorney can help gather evidence — like maintenance logs or prior complaints — that speaks to that notice requirement.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help make sure your share of fault isn't overstated.

items.question: I fell at a store off SR-99 in Biggs — do I have a case?
items.answer: It depends on whether the store knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An independent attorney can review the details, including any surveillance footage or maintenance records, and tell you honestly where you stand. There's no cost to have that conversation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity (like a city-owned sidewalk) often have a much shorter deadline. Waiting can also mean lost evidence, so it's worth acting sooner rather than later.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall in a small town like Biggs?
items.answer: Take photos of exactly where and why you fell, get names and numbers of anyone who saw it, and ask the property or store to preserve any camera footage in writing. Seek medical attention even if you feel okay at first, since some injuries show up later. Then consider getting a free case review before talking to any insurance adjuster.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with them.
